submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on the token that sits inside a multi-token unit rather than at its edge: the symbol that joins a time, range, path or hyphenated numeral compound (':' in 08:28:43 or HH:mm:ss, '-' in two-year-old or long-term, '/' in www.boost.org/libs/mpl), and the word that continues a stored technical, legal or formatting term after a noun (' of' after time/hour/year/Journal, ' for' after motion/reason/case, ' to' after motion/response or after a numeral range, ' by' after Comment, ' as' in 'well as'). It is near zero on sentence-level punctuation ('.', ',', ';', ')'), on digits and determiners, and on ordinary generated prose or common partitive phrases ('the cat sat', 'walked to', 'part of', 'end of', 'kind of', 'of course'); a few isolated peaks (e.g. ' you', Thai byte noise) are unexplained leftovers.

rival_explanations: It is only a character/token-identity detector for ':' and '-' (plus '/'), firing wherever those characters appear, so a prose colon such as 'the following:' or a lone hyphen should fire as strongly as a timestamp colon; it also cannot explain the ' of'/' for' peaks at all.

It is a technical-register detector that marks code, logs, tables and references, so it should fire broadly across such documents (on identifiers, digits and keywords as much as on joining characters) instead of only on the joining tokens; prose scientific text without notation should stay silent.

It is a low-surprisal/confidence detector that fires on tokens the model finds easy to predict and suppresses surprising ones, so any highly predictable glue token should fire (' of' after 'kind', ' the' after 'of', keyword tokens in code), regardless of whether it joins parts of a stored unit.

top_examples.text:
THE DIFFERENT TYPES OF SURGICAL GLOVES
Surgical gloves were first introduced into medical practice in 1894, and since then many different types of gloves have been developed and adapted to utilize a variety of materials for various uses.
While rubber surgical gloves may have initially been introduced for surgery, they are now a critical part of the health and safety requirements for health professionals, as well as a variety of other industries and trades.
Different Types Of Gloves
As a result of changes in healthcare requirements, availability of materials, and production opportunities, there are now a plethora of options available for disposable gloves. While most rubber gloves will be similar in appearance, the best glove for the job will typically be dependent on the particular use case, medical considerations, or just plain personal preferences of the person wearing them.
Here are some of the most common types of surgical gloves and the pros and cons of using each specific type.
The most popular option for surgical gloves today is Nitrile gloves. Nitrile is a synthetic rubber that has many properties making them ideal for industrial uses well beyond gloves. They are of higher quality than most other disposable gloves.
Nitrile rubber is more resistant than natural rubber to oils, chemicals, and acids, and has superior strength. This makes them less resistant to tearing and through manufacturing improvements they are also puncture-resistant. Keep in mind, along with the added strength and thickness, they can be less flexible than other types of rubber gloves.
They are also allergy-free, unlike latex gloves which many people have an allergy to. This makes them the preferred disposable glove for all manner of industries: automotive mechanics, tattoo artists, chemical and nuclear engineers, and of course all manner of medical professionals and doctors.
Latex gloves are often what first comes to mind when people think of disposable gloves. For many years, latex gloves were the standard in the medical field as well as a variety of other industries.
If they were the standard for so long, why were latex gloves replaced by nitrile gloves as the new favorite? The main reason is the increasing prevalence of latex allergies. While latex gloves are often preferred in terms of elasticity, comfort, and fit, medical professionals can't risk using gloves that might cause an allergic reaction in their patients.
Plasticized PVC or Vinyl is also a common material used in surgical gloves. Because vinyl gloves offer less flexibility and elasticity than other types of gloves, guidelines typically recommend either latex or nitrile gloves for clinical care and procedures that require manual dexterity and/or that involve patient contact for more than a short period of time.
Vinyl gloves show poor resistance to many chemicals, including glutaraldehyde-based products and alcohols used in the formulation of disinfectants for swabbing down work surfaces or in hand rubs.

What is Paisley Farm? Where are you located?
Paisley Farm is a family owned and operated vegetable business that was started back in 1945, in Willoughby, Ohio. Ever since 1945 and through today, we continue to make our products out of the freshest ingredients, delivered with the most exciting and flavorful taste combinations imaginable. Give us a try, we know you’ll love it!
Where are Paisley Farm vegetables grown?
We are proud to have begun as a family farm; however, we’ve outgrown our farm and we now work with family farms across the United States to make our foods.
I normally buy your Five Bean Salad at Sam’s Club, why can’t I find it right now?
In most of the club stores, Five Bean Salad is a seasonal item. If your local Club carries our Five Bean Salad they will have our bean salad from late March through August/September. Select Wal-Mart stores carry our Five Bean Salad year-round. Look for us in the canned bean aisle.
I normally buy your Four Bean Salad at Costco, why can’t I find it right now?
Why doesn’t my Costco/Sam’s Club carry your bean salad?
Paisley Farm would love to have our delicious foods in all locations but that decision is also up to the retailer. Take a moment and fill out the cards in the suggestions box located at each club store. Their managers review those comments daily and take their customers’ wants seriously, let them know you would like to see Paisley Farm on their shelves.
What is the best buy date of an unopened jar?
All Paisley Farm 16oz items have the sell by date printed on the outside rim of the lid. All 35.5oz items have the sell by date printed on the upper glass portion of the jar. The sell by date is considered the best buy date.
What is the shelf life of your items after opening?
Yes, we are proud to say that all of our products are gluten free.
What is the difference between Paisley Farm Four Bean Salad and Five Bean Salad?
The recipe is the same except our Five Bean Salad has an added pinto bean. The other four beans that you will find in both recipes are kidney, garbanzo, green, and wax beans accented with freshly diced onions and red peppers. The convenient straight from the jar goodness makes this one of our most popular items.
or call us at 1.800.474.5688 Ext. 5332. We are here Monday – Friday.

#ifndef __PROBES_COMMON_H
#define __PROBES_COMMON_H

#include <asm/inst.h>

int __insn_is_compact_branch(union mips_instruction insn);

static inline int __insn_has_delay_slot(const union mips_instruction insn)
{
	switch (insn.i_format.opcode) {
	/*
	 * jr and jalr are in r_format format.
	 */
	case spec_op:
		switch (insn.r_format.func) {
		case jalr_op:
		case jr_op:
			return 1;
		}
		break;

	/*
	 * This group contains:
	 * bltz_op, bgez_op, bltzl_op, bgezl_op,
	 * bltzal_op, bgezal_op, bltzall_op, bgezall_op.
	 */
	case bcond_op:
		switch (insn.i_format.rt) {
		case bltz_op:
		case bltzl_op:
		case bgez_op:
		case bgezl_op:
		case bltzal_op:
		case bltzall_op:
		case bgezal_op:
		case bgezall_op:
		case bposge32_op:
			return 1;
		}
		break;

	/*
	 * These are unconditional and in j_format.
	 */
	case jal_op:
	case j_op:
	case beq_op:
	case beql_op:
	case bne_op:
	case bnel_op:
	case blez_op: /* not really i_format */
	case blezl_op:
	case bgtz_op:
	case bgtzl_op:
		return 1;

	/*
	 * And now the FPA/cp1 branch instructions.
	 */
	case cop1_op:
#ifdef CONFIG_CPU_CAVIUM_OCTEON
	case lwc2_op: /* This is bbit0 on Octeon */
	case ldc2_op: /* This is bbit032 on Octeon */
	case swc2_op: /* This is bbit1 on Octeon */
	case sdc2_op: /* This is bbit132 on Octeon */
#endif
		return 1;
	}

	return 0;
}

#endif  /* __PROBES_COMMON_H */

ονσερβατόριο του Βερολίνου υπό τους Hermann Weissenborn και Gerty König. Η καριέρα της ξεκίνησε με αργά βήματα, αρχικά με ένα μικρό ρόλο το 1962 στην Deutsche Oper (ως Κέιτ Πίνκερτον στη «Μαντάμα Μπατερφλάι» του Πουτσίνι), ενώ την επόμενη χρονιά συμμετείχε στη χορωδία της Würzburg Opera.

Τραγούδησε για μικρότερους θιάσους στη Γερμανία στα μέσα της δεκαετίας του 1960 και κατόπιν με την Frankfurt am Main Opera από το 1968 μέχρι το 1971. Το 1968 πραγματοποίησε το ντεμπούτο της στη Μητροπολιτική Όπερα της Νέας Υόρκης, στο ρόλο της Wellgunde, στο έργο «Ο Χρυσός του Ρήνου» (Das Rheingold) του Βάγκνερ. Κατά τη διάρκεια της παραμονής της στη Φρανκφούρτη, άρχισε να εμφανίζεται συχνά στη Βιέννη και το Σάλτσμπουργκ, καθώς και σε άλλες μεγάλες πόλεις της Γερμανίας.

Οι εμφανίσεις της στη Μητροπολιτική Όπερα έγιναν συχνότερες κατά τη δεκαετία του 1970 και στην πρώιμη δεκαετία του 1980. Ερμήνευσε οκτώ διαφορετικούς ρόλους εκεί κατά τη διάρκεια της περιόδου αυτής, και οι εμφανίσεις της κυρίως, ως Λιου, στην «Τουραντώ» του Πουτσίνι, ως Βασίλισσα της Νύχτας, στο «Μαγικό Αυλό» του Μότσαρτ, και ως Δόννα Άννα στον «Ντον Τζοβάνι» του Μότσαρτ, έγιναν δεκτές με μεγάλους επαίνους. Ο τελευταίος ρόλος έγινε κάτι σαν το σήμα κατατεθέν της στο κοινό της Νέας Υόρκης: ερμήνευσε τη Δόννα Άννα πάμπολες φορές στη Μητροπολιτική Όπερα, 48 στον αριθμό, περισσότερες από οποιαδήποτε καλλιτέχνιδα στην ιστορία. readings.explanation: Fires on the token that sits inside a multi-token unit rather than at its edge: the symbol that joins a time, range, path or hyphenated numeral compound (':' in 08:28:43 or HH:mm:ss, '-' in two-year-old or long-term, '/' in www.boost.org/libs/mpl), and the word that continues a stored technical, legal or formatting term after a noun (' of' after time/hour/year/Journal, ' for' after motion/reason/case, ' to' after motion/response or after a numeral range, ' by' after Comment, ' as' in 'well as'). It is near zero on sentence-level punctuation ('.', ',', ';', ')'), on digits and determiners, and on ordinary generated prose or common partitive phrases ('the cat sat', 'walked to', 'part of', 'end of', 'kind of', 'of course'); a few isolated peaks (e.g. ' you', Thai byte noise) are unexplained leftovers.

It is only a character/token-identity detector for ':' and '-' (plus '/'), firing wherever those characters appear, so a prose colon such as 'the following:' or a lone hyphen should fire as strongly as a timestamp colon; it also cannot explain the ' of'/' for' peaks at all.

It is a technical-register detector that marks code, logs, tables and references, so it should fire broadly across such documents (on identifiers, digits and keywords as much as on joining characters) instead of only on the joining tokens; prose scientific text without notation should stay silent.

It is a low-surprisal/confidence detector that fires on tokens the model finds easy to predict and suppresses surprising ones, so any highly predictable glue token should fire (' of' after 'kind', ' the' after 'of', keyword tokens in code), regardless of whether it joins parts of a stored unit.
